content: Dropwort (Filipendula vulgaris), also referred to as Fern-leaf Dropwort, is a perennial herb belonging to the Rosaceae family and is closely related to Meadowsweet. This plant is commonly found in dry pastures across much of Europe, as well as central and northern Asia. The plant is characterized by its finely divided, basal leaves that resemble ferns in appearance. It grows an upright stem that reaches a height of 50 to 80 cm, which supports a loose terminal inflorescence composed of small white flowers. These tiny flowers are arranged in dense clusters and typically bloom from late spring to mid-summer. Dropwort thrives in conditions ranging from full sun to partial shade. It demonstrates a higher tolerance for dry conditions compared to most other species within its genus. Cultivation and Uses A decoction made from the roots of Dropwort has been traditionally used to treat kidney-related ailments. Additionally, it has been employed as an expectorant. The plant is propagated through seeds or by dividing its creeping root system.
